title: Experiments on parochial altruism in humans: procedures and instructions
protocol: Gather all participants in a group for preliminary verbal instructions about the general experimental procedures and game structure.
Ensure that participants do not communicate about the game before participating.
Explain the detailed rules of the game individually after each participant enters the experiment room.
Include information about the participant's role and the group affiliation of other players during individual explanations.
Use coins and cups to demonstrate the roles of players A, B, and C for clarity.
Ask test questions to ensure participants understand the instructions before proceeding with the experiment.
Make decisions on how much of the endowment to transfer to player B.
Indicate willingness to spend K0, K1, or K2 on punishment for each feasible transfer by player A before knowing the actual transfer level.
Elicit 11 punishment decisions from each player C, one for each feasible transfer level.
Elicit every player A's and every player C's expectation about punishment for transfers of K0, K5, and K10.
Conduct the games first with the Ngenikas.
Conduct the games with the Wolimbkas after completing the session with the Ngenikas.
Pay the Wolimbka participants their money immediately after everyone in the session has made a decision.
Return to the Ngenikas and pay them according to the Wolimbkas' decisions.
Explain which decisions had been made when paying each Ngenika.
Hand over the payment in envelopes to the Ngenikas.
Give each Ngenika K2 as a thank you for coming a second time.
Provide preliminary verbal instructions as a group.
Separate participants into individual rooms one by one.
Explain that the experiment may take up to 4 hours.
Inform participants about the rules and objectives of the experiment.
Clarify that any money earned during the experiments belongs to them to keep.
Distribute K3 from Assistant 1 to each participant as a thank you for their participation.
Reiterate that the distributed K3 is not part of the experiment and is theirs to keep.
